description: Remembers the git HEAD at the start of a session, and takes git snapshots of the working tree at each prompt and answer (a temporary index and refs/keepplain/<session>; your branch, index and files are not touched), so /keepplain:build can show which code each turn changed and what you changed by hand. When auto mode is on for this computer (/keepplain:auto), sends the session in the background while it runs (every five minutes of work, checked after each answer and, without holding the agent up, after each tool call), when it ends, and at the next start if it never said it ended; otherwise sends nothing. Once per session, when the agent used Builds from the KeepPlain library and the session changed code, the Stop hook shows you a line suggesting to share it (it sends nothing; KEEPPLAIN_NUDGE=0 turns it off). In a repository with your team's rules (keepplain use --team), the SessionStart hook says in one line when the team changed them, and checks the site for that in the background at most every six hours (it never rewrites the block). It also adds your KeepPlain rules to the session's context: the ones for every session at its start, and a stack's rules with the prompt they matter for (matched on this computer: the prompt goes nowhere) (and your team's in its repositories, when the team turns that on), from what a background fetch kept at most an hour ago; nothing is written into the repository, and `keepplain rules off` stops it. When a usage limit of this account passes 90% (the hooks module reads the figures Claude Code shows in its status line; nothing leaves the computer), or a turn ends on the limit (StopFailure), it offers once to continue in another agent installed on this computer: a brief of the session (task, what was done and checked, where it stopped) built here without a model, put in your clipboard and a file, with the command that starts that agent on it. `keepplain handoff off` or KEEPPLAIN_HANDOFF=0 turns the offer off. Only after `keepplain limits install`, the hooks module also keeps the two limit windows' percent after each step of the model in a file on this computer, for `keepplain limits fit` (nothing leaves the computer; `keepplain limits uninstall` stops it).
